note: When a single measurement is old enough to say so beside it. This is about the age of a reading, which is different from whether its source is responding - that lives in data/status.json.
why_absolute_rather_than_cadence_scaled: Source staleness is scaled by each source's publishing rhythm, because a monthly source is not late on day eight. A measurement is different: it does not become current again because its publisher shipped something else today. Epoch publishes daily, so scaling by cadence would mark every reading older than four days as degraded - which is most of them - and a warning that is always on stops being a signal.
calibration: Measured over the 286 dated score rows on 2026-07-29: median 34 days, p75 89, p90 233, oldest 358. The warning tier catches the 15% beyond 180 days; the stale tier catches the worst 5%.
overrides_note: Per-benchmark overrides go here when one is known to age faster or slower than the rest, keyed by benchmark_id with the same two fields.
